text: [SAMPLE / DEMO DATA - Fictional Institute of Technology] [This document is fictional and created only to demonstrate MiniRAG.] ACADEMIC RULES - FICTIONAL INSTITUTE OF TECHNOLOGY 1. Attendance Requirement Students must maintain a minimum of 75% attendance in each course during a semester to be eligible to appear for the end-semester examination. Students falling between 65% and 75% attendance may apply for condonation through the department office, subject to a valid medical or personal reason supported by documentation. 2. Grading System The institute follows a 10-point grading scale. Grades range from O (Outstanding, 90-100 marks) down to F (Fail, below 40 marks). A student's Semester Grade Point Average (SGPA) is calculated as the credit-weighted average of grade points across all courses registered in that semester. 3. Credit Requirements Undergraduate students must complete a minimum of 160 credits over eight semesters to be eligible for graduation. At least 20 of these credits must come from open elective courses outside the student's core department. 4. Re-registration and Backlogs A student who fails a core course must re-register for that course the next time it is offered. A maximum of two backlog courses may be carried forward into the final year; students with more than two backlogs will not be permitted to register for final-year core courses. 5. Class Conduct Students are expected to attend classes on time. Repeated late entry (more than 10 minutes after the scheduled start, three or more times in a month) may result in the student being marked absent for that session at the instructor's discretion. 6. Academic Integrity Any form of plagiarism, unauthorized collaboration during individual assessments, or impersonation during examinations is treated as a serious academic integrity violation and is referred to the Academic Discipline Committee.

[SAMPLE / DEMO DATA - Fictional Institute of Technology] [This document is fictional and created only to demonstrate MiniRAG.] EXAMINATION POLICY - FICTIONAL INSTITUTE OF TECHNOLOGY 1. Examination Structure Each course is assessed through a combination of Continuous Assessment (40% of total marks, covering quizzes, assignments and a mid-semester test) and an End-Semester Examination (60% of total marks). A student must score at least 30% in the End-Semester Examination independently, in addition to an overall passing score, to clear the course. 2. Examination Hall Rules Students must carry their institute identity card to every examination. Electronic devices, including smartwatches and mobile phones, are strictly prohibited inside the examination hall. Students arriving more than 30 minutes after the start of an examination will not be permitted entry. 3. Re-evaluation Requests Students who wish to have their answer script re-evaluated must submit a written request to the Controller of Examinations within 7 working days of result declaration, along with the prescribed re-evaluation fee. Re-evaluation results are final and cannot be further contested. 4. Supplementary Examinations Students who fail a course in the regular end-semester examination are eligible to appear for a supplementary examination, typically conducted within 4-6 weeks of result declaration. A student may attempt a maximum of three supplementary attempts for a single course. 5. Malpractice During Examinations Any student found using unauthorized material, communicating with another candidate, or engaging in impersonation during an examination will have their examination for that course cancelled immediately and the matter will be referred to the Examination Malpractice Committee. A first-time malpractice case may result in cancellation of that one examination; repeated offenses can lead to suspension for up to one academic year. 6. Grade Improvement A student may register to retake a course once, purely for grade improvement, even after passing it, provided they have not exhausted their maximum permissible course attempts. Only the higher of the two grades is considered in the final transcript.

[SAMPLE / DEMO DATA - Fictional Institute of Technology] [This document is fictional and created only to demonstrate MiniRAG.] SCHOLARSHIP POLICY - FICTIONAL INSTITUTE OF TECHNOLOGY 1. Merit Scholarship Students who achieve a Cumulative Grade Point Average (CGPA) of 9.0 or above at the end of an academic year are eligible for the Merit Scholarship, which waives 50% of tuition fees for the following academic year. Eligibility is reassessed annually. 2. Need-Based Financial Aid Students whose family income is below the threshold defined by the institute's Financial Aid Committee (currently updated each year) may apply for need-based financial aid covering up to 75% of tuition fees. Applications must be submitted with supporting income documentation within the first month of the academic year. 3. Sports Scholarship Students who represent the institute at state or national level in a recognized sport, and who maintain a minimum CGPA of 6.0, are eligible for a Sports Scholarship covering hostel fees for the academic year in which the representation occurred. 4. Scholarship Renewal Conditions All scholarships are renewed annually and are contingent on maintaining both the required academic performance (CGPA) and a minimum attendance of 75%, in line with the institute's general academic rules. A scholarship will be withdrawn if a student is found responsible for an academic integrity violation. 5. Application Process Scholarship applications are submitted online through the student portal. The Scholarship Committee reviews applications within 4 weeks and communicates the decision via the student's registered institute email address. Appeals against a rejected application may be filed within 2 weeks of the decision. 6. Combining Scholarships A student may hold only one primary scholarship (Merit, Need-Based, or Sports) at a time. However, a student may additionally apply for one-time book grants or conference travel grants, which are not considered primary scholarships and can be combined with any of the above.
